# ADR 0019 — The asset pipeline is an app of the hexagon

> **In short.** In the context of office assets that image and video models draw and that the office composes at
> runtime, facing generation tools that would otherwise grow as loose scripts beside the architecture, we decided to
> split the pipeline along the hexagon, with its own app, and against a standalone tools folder or build script, to
> keep what an asset is testable and shared with the office, accepting a port and an adapter per tool.

## Context and problem

Characters, their wardrobe and later the furniture are drawn by image models, animated by a local video model and cut
into layers colored at runtime ([ADR 0022](0022-assets-are-drawn-from-our-own-templates-and-checked-by-eye.md)). The
office composes them at runtime: it picks the trouser drawn for the shoe class worn, lays a skirt over the shoes and
under a jacket, and recolors only the pixels marked as the garment's main color. ADR 0011 names three apps; a generator
has no place there. The office needs the same facts about an asset that the generator produces, and the tools differ in
language and runtime: a model run as a local process, an outside image service through its official command line, image
steps written in Python.

## Decision drivers

- The generator must not break out of the architecture (maintainer, 2026-10-04 and 2026-10-12).
- What an asset is has to be the same for the generator, the office and a later asset viewer.
- Only one place may know a generation tool, so another tool can replace it.

## Considered options

- **A — An app of the hexagon:** the asset model in the core, one adapter per tool in infrastructure, the manifest in
  protocol, the workspace package `apps/asset-pipeline` that wires them.
- **B — A standalone build script or tools folder** outside the packages, which calls the tools and writes files.
- **C — Skills with loose scripts:** the steps as skills, each calling a script of its own.

## Decision

Chosen: **A**, because only it keeps the asset model in one tested place that the office and the generator share.

1. **What an asset is lives in the core.** Kind, parts with their layer order, color slots and the main-color mark,
   variants per meeting place (a trouser per shoe class, hair under a hat), anchor, footprint in tiles, directions and
   animations with their frames are domain types in `packages/core`, with the use cases that build and validate an
   asset set and the ports for generating, cutting and storing it. `[Lint import zones]`
2. **Only an adapter knows a generation tool.** The image model, the video model, the outside image service and the
   image steps (cut by key, main-color mark, recolor) live in `packages/infrastructure` behind the core's ports. A
   Python step lies beside its adapter as that adapter's internals and is started as a process; the core never starts
   a process. `[Lint import zones · Hook architecture-guard]`
3. **The office reads assets only through the manifest.** The manifest's shape is a schema in `packages/protocol`; it
   carries layers, color slots and variants as data, so the office and a viewer compose any combination without the
   core and without a new render. `[Lint import zones]`
4. **`apps/asset-pipeline` is the composition root and the command line.** It is a workspace package like the other
   apps and stands under the same import zones; every step a skill names is one of its commands.
   `[Config pnpm-workspace.yaml · Lint import zones]`

### Consequences

- Good, because a planted process call in the core turns lint red from the first line on.
- Good, because the office and the generator cannot disagree about a layer order or a color slot.
- Bad, because a tool needs a port, an adapter and a command instead of one script.
- Bad, because a Python step is a second language beside TypeScript; ADR 0007 keeps hooks and gates in TypeScript,
  and this decision admits Python only as an adapter's internals, tested through that adapter's spec.

### Confirmation

`scripts/probe-architecture.sh` turns red on `node:child_process` in the core, and `scripts/probe-lint.sh` turns red on
`node:fs` in the core and green on `apps/asset-pipeline` importing infrastructure. The guarded render port is the first
adapter, specified with a fake process; every further tool arrives as a port with an in-memory fake and an adapter with
its spec.

## Rejected

- **B — a standalone build script or tools folder.** It would hold its own idea of an asset beside the office's,
  untested by the core's fakes and outside every import zone.
- **C — skills with loose scripts.** A skill states the steps and their checks; the scripts behind it would be B.
- **Blender as the generation tool.** The rebuild by eye did not reach the approved look (ADR 0022).
